'''Aïda Beatrijs “Ietje” Paalman-de Miranda''' (20 February 1936 &ndash; 11 May 2020) was a [[Suriname]]se-born [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[mathematician]] and [[full professor]].

She was born in [[Flora, Suriname#Uitvlugt|Uitvlugt]], [[Paramaribo]].<ref name=album/> When she was 17 years old she moved from [[Suriname]] to the Netherlands to study mathematics at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. In that era, it was very unusual to study mathematics and she was the only woman at the [[Faculty (division)|faculty]]. She graduated [[cum laude]] on 23 November 1960. She started a [[PhD]] with [[Johannes de Groot]] as her supervisor. She defended her PhD thesis "Topological Semigroups" and obtained her degree in 1960, also [[cum laude]]. In 1980 she became a [[full professor]] in pure mathematics, becoming the first female full professor of mathematics in Amsterdam.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|author=Margriet van der Heijden|url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2020/05/20/ze-hield-zielsveel-van-zuivere-wiskunde-a4000353|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607073732/https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2020/05/20/ze-hield-zielsveel-van-zuivere-wiskunde-a4000353|title=Ze hield zielsveel van zuivere wiskunde|language=Dutch|website=NRC|date=20 May 2020|archive-date=7 June 2020}}</ref>

== Research ==
Paalman's research was foremost in [[topology]] and set theory. She was the PhD advisor of three students, co-advised by [https://staff.fnwi.uva.nl/j.vanmill/ Jan van Mill].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=48483|title=Aida Paalman-de Miranda |access-date=2021-01-27|website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> She published a book (''Topological semigroups - Mathematical Centre Tracts'', 1964, Mathematisch Centrum, Amsterdam) and 11 research papers about  W-groups, topological representations of semi-groups and about compact groups.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/paalman_aida.html|title=Aida Paalman|access-date=2021-01-27|author=Scott W. Williams (thanks to Jan Aarts)|date=|website=Mathematicians of the African Diaspora - Black women in Mathematics}}</ref> Paalman was also the author of numerous lecture notes for the courses she taught at the Korteweg-de Vries Institute for Mathematics at the  University of Amsterdam.

==Personal==
She married Dolf Paalman (chief [[pharmacist]]). They had two children and three grand children.<ref name="auto"/>
